If you look at the sample size of each of these polls (~400) and the fact that many of these polls were self-selecting, I doubt the viability of them through sample error and push-polling.

400 is a big enough sample. For the Central Limit Theorem to apply, you just need to expect 10 "success" and "failures" for any particular proportion you want to estimate. So if the actual support for any candidate is at least 2.5% and at most 97.5%, 400 is enough for the distribution of survey results to be approximately normal, and the margin of error of the poll to be meaningful.

Your point about non-response bias is reasonable. I didn't see anything to indicate the polls were self-selecting, but if they were, their results cannot be taken completely seriously, as respondents may in a subset of the population that feels differently than the population as a whole.
